blogs.title: Beyond Type 1 vs Type 2: Recognizing HNF1A-MODY at the bedside
blogs.description: Walk through a pragmatic diagnostic approach to young-onset, non-ketotic hyperglycaemia with glycosuria and a strong autosomal-dominant family history. We’ll dissect how fasting/stimulated C-peptide, negative GAD/IA-2/ZnT8 antibodies, post-OGTT hyperglycaemia, and clinical context separate MODY from type 1 and type 2 diabetes. We’ll also discuss the limitations of BMI and metabolic syndrome in modern cohorts, and how the Exeter MODY probability calculator may miscalibrate in non-White populations.

blogs.title: From Variant to Verdict: Applying ACMG to a novel HNF1A mutation
blogs.description: Use the case’s c.809A>G (p.N270S) HNF1A variant to illustrate bedside variant interpretation. We’ll translate ACMG criteria into clinical steps: segregation with disease, domain location (DNA-binding), in silico evidence (e.g., AlphaMissense), database absence (ClinVar/VarSome), and phenotypic fit. Practical tips on ordering NGS panels, reporting, communicating uncertainty, and cascade testing for family members are covered.

blogs.title: Precision de-escalation: When and how to stop insulin in HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: Detail a stepwise strategy to transition from initial insulin (used while awaiting diagnosis) to oral/GLP-1–based therapy after genetic confirmation. We’ll compare sulfonylureas—the classic first-line in HNF1A-MODY—versus GLP-1 receptor agonists as β-cell function declines or when hypoglycaemia risk is high, and where DPP-4 inhibitors and metformin fit. We’ll anchor these decisions to C-peptide, HbA1c trajectory, and patient-specific risks.

blogs.title: When SGLT2 bites back: Why SGLT2 inhibitors may be hazardous in HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: Explore the mechanistic link between HNF1A and SGLT2 expression, explaining the low renal glucose threshold and prominent glycosuria in HNF1A-MODY. We’ll review reports of dehydration and ketoacidosis with SGLT2 inhibitors in this genotype and outline risk–benefit considerations, mitigation strategies if contemplated, and safer alternatives for cardio-metabolic benefit.

blogs.title: The sweet-pee signal: Using glycosuria as a clue to HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: Revisit urinalysis as a diagnostic clue. We’ll discuss disproportionate glycosuria for a given plasma glucose due to reduced renal glucose reabsorption in HNF1A-MODY, how to interpret this alongside OGTT results and absence of ketones, and how this finding can nudge clinicians toward genetic testing even in patients with intermediate BMI or mixed metabolic features.

blogs.title: Early nerves, early warnings? Sudomotor dysfunction in young-onset diabetes
blogs.description: Use the case’s severely reduced sudomotor conductance to examine small-fiber/autonomic findings early in non–type 1 diabetes. We’ll cover test characteristics of electrochemical skin conductance (e.g., Sudoscan), how hyperglycaemia and genotype-specific factors might contribute, and whether abnormal sudomotor results should change monitoring intensity, therapeutic aggressiveness, or prompt broader autonomic screening.
